newsitem.title: SYRIA: Egyptian premier leaves Syria after Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian premier leaves Syria after Mideast talks.

text.p: Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri left Syria on Wednesday after two days of talks with Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on the troubled Middle East peace process.

Ganzouri, accompanied by Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif, began talks on Tuesday in the Syrian Meditarranean city of Latakia, some 320 km (200 miles) north of Damascus.
"View points on all issues discussed were identical," Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said.
The Egyptian information minister said Ganzouri's visit came within the framework of continued coordination and consultations between Syria and Egypt.

The Egyptian team's visit to Syria is the first after a visit by President Hosni Mubarak to Washington during which he discussed with President Bill Clinton ways of reviving the Syrian-Israeli peace talks which broke off a year ago.
It also follows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, which was condemned by Arab states.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but the negotiations stalled over the fate of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Syria strongly condemned Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab lands for peace and refrained from holding any talks with his government, which took over in June.
